summary: Five substantial sessions now include spontaneous role-play giving advice about moving abroad, social integration, loneliness and family boundaries. The 2026-10-14 session sustained several extended, unscripted explanations, showed independent repair of 'he have' to 'he has', and added evidence of hypothetical-advice tense instability. Working range remains A2+ / emerging B1 with medium confidence; pronunciation remains unassessed without acoustic evidence.

range.note: Spontaneously discusses social situations, AI in education, software, abstract personal motives, relocation and family boundaries, often using reasons and practical examples.

accuracy.note: Frequent he have/he has repairs confirm agreement instability; real/hypothetical forms 'I will' vs 'I would' also need more consistent control. Meaning remains understandable.

fluency.note: Sustained several multi-sentence 30–60 second explanations in a relocation/advice role-play, but pauses and restart chains are still frequent; independent self-repair helps maintain meaning.

interaction.note: Requests clarification, manages the direction and pace of the conversation, and explicitly asks the coach to maintain conversational momentum.

coherence.note: Proposed a staged one-month visit, support from a companion, gradual independence and building a social circle; articulated reasons behind setting boundaries.

pronunciation_intelligibility.note: No durable pronunciation claim: the available closeout evidence is transcript-based rather than acoustic.

active_vocabulary.note: Can produce everyday advice vocabulary, though searched for 'remind him' and 'don't back down' in a fresh interpersonal scenario.

repair_ability.note: Independently repaired 'he have' to 'he has' and rephrased several incomplete ideas while sustaining meaning.

spontaneous_complexity.note: Extended independent reasoning about loneliness, regret, guilt, autonomy, family reactions and practical plans for moving abroad.

transfer.note: New relocation role-play confirms sustained reasoning transfers beyond academic/personal-development domains; subject-verb agreement still inconsistent, and hypothetical 'would' not reliably transferred.

strengths.label: Keeps communication going by reformulating, clarifying and describing around missing words.
Actively signals misunderstanding and redirects the conversation when a topic or question is not working.

recurring_weaknesses.pattern: Frequent restart chains and fillers while assembling spontaneous sentences.
recurring_weaknesses.note: Observed across four substantial sessions. On 2026-10-13 long turns were sustained successfully, but restart chains and fillers remained frequent.

recurring_weaknesses.pattern: Lexical retrieval gaps lead to Spanish-influenced forms or repeated circumlocution.
recurring_weaknesses.note: Lexical search still appears in abstract speech, although circumlocution and self-repair increasingly preserve the message.

recurring_weaknesses.pattern: Present-tense subject-verb agreement is unstable in spontaneous speech.
recurring_weaknesses.note: 2026-10-14 fresh-country-advice role-play showed recurrent 'he have' beginnings followed by independent repairs to 'he has', alongside correct spontaneous agreement. Still unstable, with improving repair.

recurring_weaknesses.pattern: Comparative forms for short adjectives are unstable in spontaneous comparison (e.g. easier/simpler/shorter).
recurring_weaknesses.note: The pattern recurred in a fresh personal-development context after the earlier networking/design examples, so it is now a recurring rather than single-session pattern.

vocabulary.meaning: retroceder / tomar distancia en una interacción

current_priorities: Improve third-person singular control without disrupting spontaneous speech (he has / he wants / he doesn't).
Keep real versus hypothetical advice consistent (I will vs I would; if he asked, I would tell him).
Sustain extended answers with fewer restart chains, while activating useful interpersonal chunks like remind someone and don't back down.

quests.title: Steady one-minute answer
quests.description: Give a fresh one-minute answer at a controlled pace, prioritizing continuity over Spanish-like speed.
quests.evidence: Explained IPv6 for about a minute using a house-address analogy and maintained the communicative thread despite lexical search.

quests.title: Third-person control
quests.description: Tell or explain something about another person in a fresh context while keeping he/she agreement stable.

evidence_notes: Four substantial naturalistic sessions completed: 2026-09-28, 2026-10-06, 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-13.
The working CEFR range remains A2+ / B1 emerging; confidence is now medium because another varied spontaneous session supported the same range rather than a level change.
Pronunciation/intelligibility remains unscored in durable state because acoustic evidence was not available to this closeout.
2026-10-13 provided fresh-domain evidence through extended self-reflection about capability, competition, belonging, respect and relationships.
The session confirmed recurring transfer problems with present-tense agreement and short-adjective comparatives, while repair ability remained a clear strength.

2026-10-14 substantial role-play covered relocation and loneliness, staged moving plans and firm but respectful family boundaries; learner produced multi-sentence explanations and some 30–60 second turns.

Agreement self-repair recurred in a new context ('he have' -> 'he has'); spontaneous hypothetical advice often used will instead of would. Lexical search produced candidate high-reuse chunks for 'remind him' and 'don't back down'.
working_cefr_evidence: Across five varied spontaneous sessions, the learner sustains explanations, opinion defense, reformulation and interpersonal advice, including abstract and unfamiliar scenarios. 2026-10-14 confirmed developing B1-like extended speech but recurring agreement, hypothetical tense choice and pauses mean the working A2+ / B1 emerging range is unchanged; audio pronunciation remains unassessed.

be good/bad with directions; have a good/bad sense of direction
be close to someone / know someone well enough
